_README: How the automation finds each NS Retail control.
Tracked in git: no paths, no credentials - only control identities.
The routine, as performed by the operator:
Reports -> Stock Reports -> Purchases -> set the date -> F3 ->
tick every column -> Apply and Search -> Report ->
Export To... -> CSV File -> OK -> type the file name -> Save
NS Retail keeps its dialogs INSIDE the main form rather than as top-level
windows, so most windows here use "inside": "main" with an auto_id.
VERIFIED = run against the real application. CONFIRMED = read from an
inspection. TODO = still needs a capture.

windows._comment: NS Retail is a WinForms MDI app (main form auto_id 'frmMain'). Screens open inside the main window and the title becomes 'Victory Bazars - [<screen>]'. The WindowsForms10 class-name suffix changes between launches - match on the title.

close_report_screens.description: CONFIRMED 2026-09-09 - each visit to Stock Reports opens ANOTHER copy of the Purchases screen without closing the previous one; three were found stacked up during testing. Two copies make every control on the screen ambiguous, so the run would stop. This closes them all first (btnClose on each screen) and is what keeps the hundredth run identical to the first.

open_stock_reports.description: VERIFIED 2026-09-09 - 'Stock Reports' button in the Reports ribbon group. Scoped to the ribbon because a second button with the same name lives in the left auto-hide panel.

targets.title: Stock Reports

select_purchase_report.description: VERIFIED 2026-09-09 live - the earlier assumption (Stock Reports opens Purchases directly) was wrong: it opens a report catalog tree (auto_id tlReport, inside dpLeft) listing 19 report types. 'Purchases' is the DataItem with value 'Purchases' inside TreeItem 'Node8' (index-based, since the row has no auto_id or stable text - its UIA Name is 'Report row 8', the visible text 'Purchases' is only in its Value property). Clicking that TreeItem loads the Purchases criteria screen. The wait below is the real safety net: if the catalog's row order ever changes, this stops loudly here instead of silently searching the wrong report. CORRECTED 2026-09-09: the wait target was 'ucPurchases', an auto_id that does not actually exist on the live screen (confirmed by a live inspection while the screen was open and fully loaded - Node8 had already been clicked successfully). The screen's real, always-present root is layoutControl1 (the same Pane that holds btnSearch/btnReport/dpTop), so the wait now targets that instead.

targets.description: 'Purchases' row in the Stock Reports catalog tree (Node8)
targets.title: Node8

select_dispatches_report.description: CONFIRMED 2026-09-09 live - the full catalog tree (auto_id tlReport) was read row by row: Node9's DataItem value is 'Dispatches'. Its criteria screen has the same dtpFromDate/dtpToDate pair as Purchases, plus extra unused filters (Branch, Periodicity, Category, Item Code). The wait target (layoutControl1) matches twice on this screen - once for the report's own root layout, once for the nested search-criteria sub-control (ucBranchTransactions) - but the 'wait' action tolerates an ambiguous match (it means the control certainly exists), so this is not a problem.

set_date.description: VERIFIED 2026-09-09 on the running application - typing '08 September 2026' into both pickers took effect. The Edit inside each picker has an automation id that is really a window handle and changes every launch, so it is found through its parent ComboBox instead.

set_as_on_date.description: Stock As on date is a snapshot report - its criteria screen has one date field (dtAsOnDate), not the dtpFromDate/dtpToDate pair the range reports use. Confirmed 2026-09-09 by live inspection of the open screen (a ComboBox with auto_id dtAsOnDate under a pane titled 'As on Date').

open_column_settings.description: VERIFIED workflow step - F3 on the Purchases screen opens the Include/Exclude column dialog. Waits for the dialog to actually appear.

include_all_columns.description: CONFIRMED 2026-09-09 - the Include/Exclude grid is a DevExpress table (gcIncExc) whose cells report 'Checked'/'Unchecked'. Only unticked rows are touched, so anything already selected stays selected, and the grid is paged through because it only loads visible rows.

targets.description: tick every column in the Include grid

apply_and_search.description: CONFIRMED 2026-09-09 - 'Apply and Search' (auto_id btnApplyAndSearch) inside the frmIncludeExclude dialog. This is what performs the search in the operator's routine - the Search button on the criteria panel is not used.

search.description: NOT USED in this workflow - the operator searches from inside the F3 dialog instead. Kept as a verified fallback: btnSearch on the criteria panel. apply_and_search takes precedence whenever it is mapped.

export_to.description: CORRECTED 2026-09-09 from a screenshot of the actual open menu (docs/captures - the operator captured it directly instead of guessing from automation). The list is a FIXED 10 entries, always in this order: PDF, HTML, MHT, RTF, DOCX, XLS, XLSX, CSV, Text, Image - CSV is always the 8th (index 7). The earlier 'most-recently-used ordering' theory was wrong; it was concluded from a trial loop whose own repeated selections were themselves corrupting later trials in ways that were never actually isolated from a stable baseline. Menu entries are still invisible to UI Automation (0 descendants under the popup's MenuBar, confirmed live), so this is a fixed keyboard position - Home, Down x7, Enter - not a read-and-match. choose_csv_format (next step) still verifies the resulting dialog really says CSV, so a future menu change fails loudly instead of silently exporting the wrong format. timeout_seconds raised to 90 on the first click after a large report (Sales, ~10k+ rows with detailed columns) made NS Retail itself go briefly unresponsive right after the Preview window appeared - confirmed live: the process stayed alive and the window came back on its own about 20-30 seconds later, it just was not ready to accept clicks yet.

targets.description: Home (sent twice to let the popup finish rendering before navigating), down to CSV (8th entry), Enter

choose_csv_format.description: CONFIRMED 2026-09-09 - checks the options dialog that export_to's menu selection opened really is 'CSV Export Options'. If the format list's entry order ever changes, the next run stops here with a clear message instead of writing e.g. an XLSX file into a .csv name.

targets.description: the export options dialog is the CSV one

confirm_export.description: CONFIRMED 2026-09-09 - OK (auto_id btnOK) in the CSV Export Options dialog. The encoding and separator are left exactly as the operator has them.

save_set_path.description: CONFIRMED 2026-09-09 - checks the dialog really is saving CSV, then types the full destination into the File name box (Edit auto_id 1001). A Windows save dialog accepts a complete path, so no folder navigation is needed; the folder is created by the automation beforehand. CORRECTED 2026-09-09: the File name target used 'set_text', whose UI-Automation ValuePattern set passed its own readback check (the box visibly showed the right path) but did NOT update the Explorer common dialog's actual committed filename - confirmed live by a 'Document.csv already exists?' prompt appearing after Save was clicked, even though the box read back the full target path. Switched to real keystrokes (select-all, then type), which this dialog does honor.

targets.description: File name (real keystrokes: select all, then type - a ValuePattern set does not update this dialog's committed filename)

save_confirm.description: CONFIRMED 2026-09-09 - the Save button (auto_id 1) in the Save As dialog. The ribbon has its own 'Save' button, so this is scoped to the dialog.

dismiss_open_prompt.description: CONFIRMED 2026-09-09 - after every export NS Retail shows its own 'Export' dialog asking 'Do you want to open this file?'. The operator's routine is to say No (the file only needs to be saved, not opened) - saying Yes would launch a viewer for it and leave that extra window open too. Marked optional: on at least one run this session it appeared, but nothing guarantees every NS Retail build/version shows it.
